title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 97 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 518–520 (Night 97, continuing directly from nights-96), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 97 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Dhāt al-Dawāhī, still taken for a holy ascetic, lays the patrician's head before the trapped Muslims and offers to slip out of the pass unseen and bring twenty thousand horsemen from their army. Sharrukān stays with his men; she leads his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān and the vizier Dandān out instead, having already told the infidels she will deliver the Muslim king to them for King Afrīdūn. The infidels let the three pass through their lines untouched, and the two men praise the ascetic's wonders, until the infidels close in and seize them. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ السَّابِعَةُ وَالتِّسْعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-sābiʿatu wa-al-tisʿūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the seventh-and-ninetieth,
sentences.i: And when it was the ninety-seventh night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ اللَّعِينَةَ ذَاتَ الدَّوَاهِي لَمَّا أَخَذَتْ رَأْسَ الْبِطْرِيقِ رَئِيسِ الْعِشْرِينَ أَلْفَ كَافِرٍ أَتَتْ بِهَا وَأَلْقَتْهَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَأَخِيهِ شَرْكَانَ وَالْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-laʿīnata dhāta al-dawāhī lammā akhadhat raʾsa al-biṭrīqi raʾīsi al-ʿishrīna alfa kāfirin atat bihā wa-alqathā bayna yaday ḍawʾi al-makāni wa-akhīhi sharrukāna wa-al-wazīri dandāna
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the accursed-one Dhāt al-Dawāhī, when she had taken the head of the patrician, chief of the twenty thousand infidels, came with it and cast it between the two hands of Ḍawʾ al-Makān and his brother Sharrukān and the vizier Dandān.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when the accursed Dhāt al-Dawāhī had taken the head of the patrician who commanded the twenty thousand infidels, she brought it and threw it down before Ḍawʾ al-Makān, his brother Sharrukān and the vizier Dandān.
sentences.n: The print has دات, a misprint for ذات, corrected here. dhāta is accusative, in apposition to al-laʿīnata after anna. As at the end of the last night, bihā and alqathā treat raʾs, “head”, as feminine; and atā bi-, “come with”, is “bring”: the verb chooses the bi-. The new night opens by retelling the scene on which the last one closed.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لَهُمْ لَمَّا رَأَيْتُ حَالَكُمْ أَخَذَتْنِي الْغَيْرَةُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَهَجَمْتُ عَلَى الْبِطْرِيقِ الْكَبِيرِ وَضَرَبْتُهُ بِالسَّيْفِ فَأَطَحْتُ رَأْسَهُ وَلَمْ يَقْدِرْ أَحَدٌ مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ أَنْ يَدْنُوَ مِنِّي وَأَتَيْتُ بِرَأْسِهِ إِلَيْكُمْ لِتَقْوَى نُفُوسُكُمْ عَلَى الْجِهَادِ وَتُرْضُوا بِسُيُوفِكُمْ رَبَّ الْعِبَادِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahum lammā raʾaytu ḥālakum akhadhatnī al-ghayratu ʿalaykum wa-hajamtu ʿalā al-biṭrīqi al-kabīri wa-ḍarabtuhu bi-al-sayfi fa-aṭaḥtu raʾsahu wa-lam yaqdir aḥadun mina al-kuffāri an yadnuwa minnī wa-ataytu bi-raʾsihi ilaykum li-taqwā nufūsukum ʿalā al-jihādi wa-turḍū bi-suyūfikum rabba al-ʿibādi
sentences.l: And she said to them: When I saw your state, the zeal for you took me, and I fell upon the great patrician and struck him with the sword and sent-flying his head; and none of the infidels was able to draw-near to me; and I came with his head to you, that your souls may grow-strong for the holy-war, and that you may please with your swords the Lord of the servants.
sentences.i: And she said to them, “When I saw the plight you were in, I was seized with zeal on your behalf. I fell upon the great patrician, struck him with my sword and sent his head flying, and not one of the infidels could come near me. I have brought you his head so that your hearts may be strengthened for the holy war, and you may please the Lord of all servants with your swords.
sentences.n: Here the narrator gives her qālat, “she said”, though in the last night, in the same scene, it was qāla, following the disguise; her own words stay those of a man. bi-al-sayfi, “with the sword”: bi- of the instrument, as in bi-suyūfikum. li-taqwā: li- “so that” governs the subjunctive, and turḍū (from arḍā, “to satisfy, please”) shares it. Sajʿ: al-jihādi/al-ʿibādi. The print spells رايت and راسه without hamza.

sentences.t: وَأُرِيدُأَنْ أَشْغَلَكُمْ فِى الْجِهَادِ وَأَذْهَبَ إِلَى عَسْكَرِكُمْ وَلَوْ كَانُوا عَلَى بَابِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ وَآتِيَكُمْ مِنْ عِنْدِهِمْ بِعِشْرِينَ أَلْفَ فَارِسٍ يُهْلِكُونَ هَؤُلَاءِ الْكَفَرَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-urīdu an ashghalakum fī al-jihādi wa-adhhaba ilā ʿaskarikum wa-law kānū ʿalā bābi al-qusṭanṭīniyyati wa-ātiyakum min ʿindihim bi-ʿishrīna alfa fārisin yuhlikūna hāʾulāʾi al-kafarata
sentences.l: And I want that I occupy you in the holy-war, and go to your army, even if they are at the gate of Constantinople, and come to you from their presence with twenty thousand horsemen who will destroy these unbelievers.
sentences.i: Now my wish is to leave you engaged in the holy war while I go to your army, even if it lies at the very gate of Constantinople, and bring you back from it twenty thousand horsemen to destroy these unbelievers.”
sentences.n: واريدان is printed as one word, for wa-urīdu an, “and I want to”. an governs three subjunctives in a row: ashghala, adhhaba, ātiya. shaghala, “to occupy, keep busy”: she means the Muslims are to hold the pass and keep fighting while she fetches help. ātī-kum … bi-, “come to you with”, is again “bring”. The army she names is the main Muslim host besieging Constantinople. فى is printed with ى for ي.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ شَرْكَانُ وَكَيْفَ تَمْضِي إِلَيْهِمْ أَيُّهَا الزَّاهِدُ وَالْوَادِي مَسْدُودٌ بِالْكُفَّارِ مِنْ كُلِّ جَانِبٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla sharrukānu wa-kayfa tamḍī ilayhim ayyuhā al-zāhidu wa-al-wādī masdūdun bi-al-kuffāri min kulli jānibin
sentences.l: And Sharrukān said: And how will you go to them, O ascetic, and the valley is blocked with the infidels on every side?
sentences.i: Sharrukān said, “But how can you reach them, holy man, when the valley is blocked by infidels on every side?”
sentences.n: wa-al-wādī masdūdun is a circumstantial clause: “while the valley is blocked”. bi-al-kuffāri: bi- names what blocks it. tamḍī and al-zāhidu are masculine: Sharrukān still takes her for a man.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْمَلْعُونَةُ اللَّهُ يَسْتُرُنِي عَنْ أَعْيُنِهِمْ فَلَا يَرَوْنِي وَمَنْ رَآنِي لَا يَجْسُرُأَنْ يُقْبِلَ عَلَيَّ فَإِنِّي فِي ذَلِكَ الْوَقْتِ أَكُونُ فَانِيًا فِي اللَّهِ وَهُوَ يُقَاتِلُ عَنِّي عِدَاةً
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-malʿūnatu allāhu yasturunī ʿan aʿyunihim fa-lā yarawnī wa-man raʾānī lā yajsuru an yuqbila ʿalayya fa-innī fī dhālika al-waqti akūnu fāniyan fī allāhi wa-huwa yuqātilu ʿannī ʿidātan
sentences.l: And the accursed-woman said: God veils me from their eyes, so they do not see me; and whoever sees me does not dare to advance upon me; for I at that time am passed-away in God, and He fights on-my-behalf enemies.
sentences.i: The accursed woman answered, “God hides me from their eyes, so that they cannot see me; and whoever does see me dare not come at me. For at such a time I am lost in God, and it is He who fights my enemies for me.”
sentences.n: يجسران is printed as one word, for yajsuru an, “dares to”. fānin fī allāhi, “passing away in God”, is the Sufi term fanāʾ, the self extinguished in God; the crone borrows the language of the saints, and fāniyan is masculine to suit the disguise. The print marks a kasra on the last word, عِداة, an unclear form: it is read here as ʿidātan, “enemies”, the object of yuqātilu ʿannī, “he fights for me”, a plural akin to ʿidan and to ʿudāt (plural of ʿādin, “enemy”). It may instead be a misprint for عِدَاهُ, “his enemies”, or عِدَاتِي, “my enemies”. The print sets the shadda of عليّ itself.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ شَرْكَانُ صَدَقْتَ أَيُّهَا الزَّاهِدُ لِأَنِّي شَاهَدْتُ ذَلِكَ وَإِذَا كُنْتَ تَقْدِرُأَنْ تَمْضِيَ أَوَّلَ اللَّيْلِ يَكُونُ ذَلِكَ أَجْوَدَ لَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla sharrukānu ṣadaqta ayyuhā al-zāhidu li-annī shāhadtu dhālika wa-idhā kunta taqdiru an tamḍiya awwala al-layli yakūnu dhālika ajwada lanā
sentences.l: And Sharrukān said: You have spoken-truly, O ascetic, for I witnessed that; and if you are able to go at the first of the night, that will be better for us.
sentences.i: “You speak the truth, holy man,” said Sharrukān, “for I saw it with my own eyes. And if you can set out at nightfall, that will be best for us.”
sentences.n: تقدران is printed as one word, for taqdiru an, “you are able to”. The answer to idhā comes without fa-: yakūnu dhālika, not fa-yakūnu, a common Middle Arabic way of joining a condition and its answer. li-annī, “because I”: li- “for, because” with anna. awwala al-layli, “at the first of the night”, is an accusative of time.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَنَا أَمْضِي فِي هَذِهِ السَّاعَةِ وَإِنْ كُنْتَ تُرِيدُأَنْ تَجِيءَ مَعِي وَلَا يَرَاكَ أَحَدٌ فَقُمْ وَإِنْ كَانَ أَخُوكَ يَذْهَبُ مَعَنَا أَخَذْنَاهُ دُونَ غَيْرِهِ فَإِنَّ ظِلَّ الْوَلِيِّ لَا يَسْتُرُ غَيْرَ اثْنَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla anā amḍī fī hādhihi al-sāʿati wa-in kunta turīdu an tajīʾa maʿī wa-lā yarāka aḥadun fa-qum wa-in kāna akhūka yadhhabu maʿanā akhadhnāhu dūna ghayrihi fa-inna ẓilla al-waliyyi lā yasturu ghayra ithnayni
sentences.l: And he said: I go in this hour; and if you want to come with me and no one sees you, then rise; and if your brother is going with us, we take him and not another, for the shadow of the saint does not veil other than two.
sentences.i: “I shall go this very hour,” came the answer. “If you wish to come with me unseen by anyone, rise. And if your brother is to come with us, we will take him and no one else, for a saint's shadow can hide no more than two.”
sentences.n: تريدان is printed as one word, for turīdu an, “you want to”. Back to fa-qāla, “he said”: the narrator again follows the disguise. walī, “friend (of God), saint”: the crone claims a saint's power to cover his companions from sight with his shadow. The answer akhadhnāhu, “we take him”, is a perfect after in, as Classical allows.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ شَرْكَانُ أَمَّا أَنَا فَلَا أَتْرُكُ أَصْحَابِي وَلَكِنْ إِذَا كَانَ أَخِي يَرْضَى بِذَلِكَ فَلَا بَأْسَ حَيْثُ ذَهَبَ مَعَكَ وَخَلَصَ مِنْ هَذَا الضِّيقِ فَإِنَّهُ هُوَ حِصْنُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَسَيْفُ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla sharrukānu ammā anā fa-lā atruku aṣḥābī wa-lākin idhā kāna akhī yarḍā bi-dhālika fa-lā baʾsa ḥaythu dhahaba maʿaka wa-khalaṣa min hādhā al-ḍīqi fa-innahu huwa ḥiṣnu al-muslimīna wa-sayfu rabbi al-ʿālamīna
sentences.l: And Sharrukān said: As for me, I do not leave my companions; but if my brother is content with that, then there is no harm, in-that he goes with you and gets-free from this strait, for he, he is the fortress of the Muslims and the sword of the Lord of the worlds.
sentences.i: Sharrukān said, “For my part, I will not leave my companions. But if my brother is willing, there is no harm in his going with you and escaping from this strait, for he is the fortress of the Muslims and the sword of the Lord of the worlds.
sentences.n: ḥaythu, properly “where”, is used here in the post-classical sense “in that, seeing that”: fa-lā baʾsa ḥaythu dhahaba, “no harm in his going”. raḍiya bi-, “be content with”: the verb chooses the bi-. Sajʿ: al-muslimīna/al-ʿālamīna. The print spells باس without hamza.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ شَاءَ فَلْيَأْخُذْ مَعَهُ الْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ أَوْ مَنْ يَخْتَارُ ثُمَّ يُرْسِلْ إِلَيْنَا عَشَرَةَ آلَافِ فَارِسٍ إِعَانَةً عَلَى هَؤُلَاءِ اللِّئَامِ
sentences.tr: wa-in shāʾa fa-l-yaʾkhudh maʿahu al-wazīra dandāna aw man yakhtāru thumma yursil ilaynā ʿasharata ālāfi fārisin iʿānatan ʿalā hāʾulāʾi al-liʾāmi
sentences.l: And if he wills, then let him take with him the vizier Dandān or whom he chooses; then let him send to us ten thousand horsemen as an aid against these base-ones.
sentences.i: If he likes, let him take the vizier Dandān with him, or whomever he chooses, and then send us ten thousand horsemen to help us against these villains.”
sentences.n: fa-l-yaʾkhudh: li- with the jussive is “let him”; yursil after thumma is read as a second jussive under the same command. The print spells فلياخذ without hamza. iʿānatan, “as an aid”, is an accusative of purpose; ʿalā, “against”. The crone offered to fetch twenty thousand horsemen; Sharrukān asks for ten.

sentences.t: فَاصْطَلَحُوا وَاتَّفَقُوا عَلَى هَذَا الْحَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-iṣṭalaḥū wa-ittafaqū ʿalā hādhā al-ḥāli
sentences.l: And they came-to-terms and agreed upon this state.
sentences.i: So they came to terms and agreed on this plan.
sentences.n: ḥāl is usually feminine, but here takes the masculine hādhā, as often in the Nights.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْعَجُوزَ قَالَتْ أَمْهِلُونِي حَتَّى أَذْهَبَ قَبْلَكُمْ وَأَنْظُرَ حَالَ الْكَفَرَةِ هَلْ هُمْ نِيَامٌ أَوْ يَقْظَانُونَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-ʿajūza qālat amhilūnī ḥattā adhhaba qablakum wa-anẓura ḥāla al-kafarati hal hum niyāmun aw yaqẓānūna
sentences.l: Then the old-woman said: Give-me-time until I go before you and look at the state of the unbelievers, whether they are sleeping or awake.
sentences.i: Then the old woman said, “Give me a little time, so that I can go ahead of you and see how the unbelievers stand, whether they are asleep or awake.”
sentences.n: The print has فيام, a misprint for نيام, corrected here. The narrator calls her al-ʿajūz, “the old woman”, while the men still see a male ascetic. yaqẓānūna is a Middle Arabic plural: Classical treats yaqẓān as a diptote adjective with the plural yaqāẓā or yuqāẓā, but the text adds the sound masculine ending -ūna; it is kept as printed. Sajʿ-like balance: niyāmun/yaqẓānūna.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا مَا نَخْرُجُ إِلَّا مَعَكَ وَنُسَلِّمُ أَمْرَنَا لِلَّهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū mā nakhruju illā maʿaka wa-nusallimu amranā li-allāhi
sentences.l: And they said: We do not go-out except with you, and we hand-over our affair to God.
sentences.i: But they said, “We will not go out except with you; we commit our fate to God.”
sentences.n: maʿaka is masculine: to them she is still the holy man. li-allāhi: li- marks to whom the matter is handed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ إِذَا طَاوَعْتُكُمْ لَا تَلُومُونِي وَلُومُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ فَالرَّأْيُ عِنْدِي أَنْ تُمْهِلُونِي حَتَّى أَكْشِفَ خَبَرَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat idhā ṭāwaʿtukum lā talūmūnī wa-lūmū anfusakum fa-al-raʾyu ʿindī an tumhilūnī ḥattā akshifa khabarahum
sentences.l: And she said: If I comply-with you, do not blame me, and blame your selves; for the opinion with me is that you give-me-time until I uncover their news.
sentences.i: She said, “If I do as you wish, do not blame me; blame yourselves. My own judgement is that you give me time to find out how things stand with them.”
sentences.n: lā talūmūnī is a prohibition, jussive talūmū plus -nī, “me”. ʿindī, “with me”, is “in my view”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ شَرْكَانُ امْضِ إِلَيْهِمْ وَلَا تُبْطِئْ عَلَيْنَا لِأَنَّنَا نَنْتَظِرُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla sharrukānu imḍi ilayhim wa-lā tubṭiʾ ʿalaynā li-annanā nantaẓiruka
sentences.l: And Sharrukān said: Go to them, and do not be-slow upon us, for we are waiting-for you.
sentences.i: “Go to them,” said Sharrukān, “and do not keep us waiting long, for we will be watching for you.”
sentences.n: abṭaʾa ʿalā, “be slow in coming back to”: the ʿalā names those left waiting. li-annanā, “because we”.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ خَرَجَتْ ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika kharajat dhātu al-dawāhī
sentences.l: And at that, Dhāt al-Dawāhī went-out.
sentences.i: With that, Dhāt al-Dawāhī went out.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ شَرْكَانُ حَدَّثَ أَخَاهُ بَعْدَ خُرُوجِهَا وَقَالَ لَوْلَا أَنَّ الزَّاهِدَ صَاحِبُ كَرَامَاتٍ مَا كَانَ قَتَلَ هَذَا الْبِطْرِيقَ الْجَبَّارَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna sharrukānu ḥaddatha akhāhu baʿda khurūjihā wa-qāla lawlā anna al-zāhida ṣāḥibu karāmātin mā kāna qatala hādhā al-biṭrīqa al-jabbāra
sentences.l: And Sharrukān talked-with his brother after her going-out, and said: Were it not that the ascetic is a possessor of saintly-wonders, he would not have killed this tyrant patrician.
sentences.i: After she had gone, Sharrukān talked with his brother. “If the holy man were not a worker of miracles,” he said, “he could never have killed this mighty patrician.
sentences.n: The print has اخاة, a misprint for اخاه, corrected here, as in the last night. karāmāt are the wonders granted to saints, as against the prophets' miracles. lawlā … mā kāna qatala, “were it not … he would not have killed”: kāna with the perfect gives the unreal past.

sentences.t: وَفِي هَذَا الْقَدْرِ كِفَايَةٌ فِي كَرَامَةِ هَذَا الزَّاهِدِ وَقَدِ انْكَسَرَتْ شَوْكَةُ الْكُفَّارِ بِقَتْلِ هَذَا الْبِطْرِيقِ لِأَنَّهُ كَانَ جَبَّارًا عَنِيدًا وَشَيْطَانًا مَرِيدًا
sentences.tr: wa-fī hādhā al-qadri kifāyatun fī karāmati hādhā al-zāhidi wa-qadi inkasarat shawkatu al-kuffāri bi-qatli hādhā al-biṭrīqi li-annahu kāna jabbāran ʿanīdan wa-shayṭānan marīdan
sentences.l: And in this measure is sufficiency concerning the saintly-wonder of this ascetic; and the thorn of the infidels has been broken by the killing of this patrician, for he was a stubborn tyrant and a rebel devil.
sentences.i: That much is proof enough of this holy man's power. And the infidels' strength is broken with the death of this patrician, for he was a stubborn tyrant and a rebellious devil.”
sentences.n: shawka, “thorn”, is also “sting, force, might”: inkasarat shawkatuhum, “their might was broken”. bi-qatli: bi- gives the cause, “by the killing”. Sajʿ: ʿanīdan/marīdan; both words echo the Qurʾān (jabbār ʿanīd, shayṭān marīd). The print sets the fatḥa of مَريدا itself.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُمْ يَتَحَدَّثُونَ فِي كَرَامَاتِ الزَّاهِدِ وَإِذَا بِاللَّعِينَةِ ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي قَدْ دَخَلَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَوَعَدَتْهُمْ بِالنَّصْرِ عَلَى الْكَفَرَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā hum yataḥaddathūna fī karāmāti al-zāhidi wa-idhā bi-al-laʿīnati dhāti al-dawāhī qad dakhalat ʿalayhim wa-waʿadathum bi-al-naṣri ʿalā al-kafarati
sentences.l: And while they were talking about the saintly-wonders of the ascetic, and behold, the accursed-one Dhāt al-Dawāhī had come-in upon them, and she promised them the victory over the unbelievers.
sentences.i: While they were still talking of the holy man's miracles, in came the accursed Dhāt al-Dawāhī, and she promised them victory over the unbelievers.
sentences.n: wa-idhā bi-: after idhā of surprise the bi- only marks what appears, “and behold, the accursed one”. waʿada bi-, “promise (something)”: the verb chooses the bi-.

sentences.t: فَشَكَرُوا الزَّاهِدَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ وَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ هَذِهِ حِيلَةٌ وَخِدَاعٌ
sentences.tr: fa-shakarū al-zāhida ʿalā dhālika wa-lam yaʿlamū anna hādhihi ḥīlatun wa-khidāʿun
sentences.l: And they thanked the ascetic for that, and they did not know that this was a trick and deceit.
sentences.i: They thanked the holy man for it, never knowing that all this was a trick and a deception.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتِ اللَّعِينَةُ أَيْنَ مَلِكُ الزَّمَانِ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ فَأَجَابَهَا بِالتَّلْبِيَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma qālati al-laʿīnatu ayna maliku al-zamāni ḍawʾu al-makāni fa-ajābahā bi-al-talbiyati
sentences.l: Then the accursed-one said: Where is the king of the age, Ḍawʾ al-Makān? And he answered her with the 'here-I-am'.
sentences.i: Then the accursed woman asked, “Where is the king of the age, Ḍawʾ al-Makān?” and he answered her with a ready “Here I am!”
sentences.n: talbiya is the answer labbayka, “at your service, here I am”, the cry of the pilgrim and of a willing servant. bi-al-talbiyati: bi- gives the manner of answering. The rhyme al-zamāni/al-makāni is the usual chime on the king's name.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ خُذْ مَعَكَ وَزِيرَكَ وَسِرْ خَلْفِي حَتَّى نَذْهَبَ إِلَى الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu khudh maʿaka wazīraka wa-sir khalfī ḥattā nadhhaba ilā al-qusṭanṭīniyyati
sentences.l: And she said to him: Take with you your vizier and travel behind me, so that we go to Constantinople.
sentences.i: She said to him, “Take your vizier with you and follow me, and we will go to Constantinople.”
sentences.n: ḥattā with the subjunctive is “so that, until”. She names Constantinople, where the main Muslim host lies; the reader already knows she has promised the infidels to deliver the king to them.

sentences.t: وَكَانَتْ ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي قَدْ أَعْلَمَتِ الْكُفَّارَ بِالْحِيلَةِ الَّتِي عَمِلَتْهَا فَفَرِحُوا بِذَلِكَ غَايَةَ الْفَرَحِ
sentences.tr: wa-kānat dhātu al-dawāhī qad aʿlamati al-kuffāra bi-al-ḥīlati allatī ʿamilathā fa-fariḥū bi-dhālika ghāyata al-faraḥi
sentences.l: And Dhāt al-Dawāhī had informed the infidels of the trick which she had done, and they rejoiced at that the utmost of the joy.
sentences.i: Now Dhāt al-Dawāhī had already told the infidels of the trick she had played, and they were overjoyed at it.
sentences.n: kānat … qad aʿlamat is a pluperfect, “had informed”. aʿlama bi-, “inform of”, and fariḥa bi-, “rejoice at”: the verbs choose the bi-. ghāyata al-faraḥi, “the utmost of joy”, is an adverbial accusative of degree.

sentences.t: وَقَالُوا مَا يَجْبُرُ خَاطِرَنَا إِلَّا قَتْلُ مَلِكِهِمْ فِي نَظِيرِ قَتْلِ الْبِطْرِيقِ لِأَنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ عِنْدَنَا أَفْرَسُ مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qālū mā yajburu khāṭiranā illā qatlu malikihim fī naẓīri qatli al-biṭrīqi li-annahu lam yakun ʿindanā afrasu minhu
sentences.l: And they said: Nothing mends our mind except the killing of their king, in counterpart to the killing of the patrician, for there was not with us a better-horseman than he.
sentences.i: And they said, “Nothing will console us but the killing of their king in return for the killing of the patrician, for we had no finer horseman than he.”
sentences.n: jabara khāṭirahu, “set his mind (as one sets a broken bone)”, is “console, comfort”. fī naẓīri, “in the counterpart of”, is “in exchange for”. afrasu, “more skilled a horseman”, is the elative of fāris.

sentences.t: وَقَالُوا لِعَجُوزِ النَّحْسِ ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي حِينَ أَخْبَرَتْهُمْ بِأَنَّهَا تَذْهَبُ إِلَيْهِمْ بِمَلِكِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ إِذَا أَتَيْتِ بِهِ نَأْخُذُهُ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ
sentences.tr: wa-qālū li-ʿajūzi al-naḥsi dhāti al-dawāhī ḥīna akhbarathum bi-annahā tadhhabu ilayhim bi-maliki al-muslimīna idhā atayti bihi naʾkhudhuhu ilā al-maliki afrīdūna
sentences.l: And they said to the old-woman of the ill-omen, Dhāt al-Dawāhī, when she informed them that she would go to them with the king of the Muslims: When you come with him, we take him to the king Afrīdūn.
sentences.i: When she told them that she would bring them the king of the Muslims, they said to that ill-starred crone Dhāt al-Dawāhī, “When you bring him, we will take him to King Afrīdūn.”
sentences.n: The print has ناخذة, a misprint for ناخذه, corrected here. ʿajūz al-naḥs, “the old woman of ill omen”: naḥs is bad luck, an evil star. tadhhabu ilayhim, “she would go to them”: dhahaba bi-, “go with”, is to take or bring, and atā bi-, “come with”, likewise “bring”; in both the verb chooses the bi-. atayti is feminine: the infidels know what she is. The print sets the kasra of لِعجوز itself.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْعَجُوزَ ذَاتَ الدَّوَاهِي تَوَجَّهَتْ وَتَوَجَّهَ مَعَهَا ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَالْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ وَهِيَ سَابِقَةٌ عَلَيْهِمَا وَتَقُولُ لَهُمَا سِيرَا عَلَى بَرَكَةِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى فَأَجَابَاهَا إِلَى قَوْلِهَا وَنَفَذَ فِيهِمَا سَهْمُ الْقَضَاءِ وَالْقَدَرِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-ʿajūza dhāta al-dawāhī tawajjahat wa-tawajjaha maʿahā ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-al-wazīru dandānu wa-hiya sābiqatun ʿalayhimā wa-taqūlu lahumā sīrā ʿalā barakati allāhi taʿālā fa-ajābāhā ilā qawlihā wa-nafadha fīhimā sahmu al-qaḍāʾi wa-al-qadari
sentences.l: Then the old-woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī set-out, and there set-out with her Ḍawʾ al-Makān and the vizier Dandān, she going-ahead of them and saying to them: Go, you-two, upon the blessing of God the Exalted! And they-two answered her to her saying, and the arrow of the decree and the destiny went-through them.
sentences.i: Then the crone Dhāt al-Dawāhī set out, and Ḍawʾ al-Makān and the vizier Dandān set out with her, she going on ahead of them and saying, “March on, with the blessing of God Most High!” They did as she said, and the arrow of fate and destiny pierced them through.
sentences.n: The print has اى, a misprint for الى, corrected here. sīrā is the dual imperative, “go, you two”. ajāba ilā, “answer to”, is to consent, to do what is asked. nafadha, of an arrow, is to pass clean through; al-qaḍāʾ wa-al-qadar, God's decree and its measuring-out, is the fixed pair for fate.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ تَزَلْ سَائِرَةً بِهِمَا حَتَّى تَوَسَّطَتْ بِهِمَا بَيْنَ عَسْكَرِ الرُّومِ وَوَصَلُوا إِلَى الشِّعْبِ الْمَذْكُورِ الضَّيِّقِ وَعَسَاكِرُ الْكُفَّارِ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَيْهِمْ وَلَا يَتَعَرَّضُونَ لَهُمْ بِسُوءٍ لِأَنَّ الْمَلْعُونَةَ أَوْصَتْهُمْ بِذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-lam tazal sāʾiratan bihimā ḥattā tawassaṭat bihimā bayna ʿaskari al-rūmi wa-waṣalū ilā al-shiʿbi al-madhkūri al-ḍayyiqi wa-ʿasākiru al-kuffāri yanẓurūna ilayhim wa-lā yataʿarraḍūna lahum bi-sūʾin li-anna al-malʿūnata awṣathum bi-dhālika
sentences.l: And she did not cease going with them till she brought-them-into-the-midst of the army of al-Rūm, and they reached the aforementioned narrow pass; and the armies of the infidels were looking at them and not meddling with them with harm, because the accursed-woman had charged them with that.
sentences.i: On she led them until she had brought them into the very midst of the army of al-Rūm, and they reached the narrow pass already spoken of. The infidel troops watched them and did not lay a hand on them, for the accursed woman had told them to let them be.
sentences.n: sāra bi-, “go with”, is to lead, and tawassaṭa bi-, “get into the middle with”, to bring into the midst. The text moves from the dual (bihimā) to the plural (waṣalū, ilayhim, lahum) as the old woman is counted in with the two men. taʿarraḍa li-, “put oneself in the way of”, is to meddle with or molest; bi-sūʾin, “with harm”. awṣā bi-, “charge with”: the verb chooses the bi-. al-shiʿb is a pass or defile between mountains.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَالْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ أَنَّ عَسَاكِرَ الْكُفَّارِ وَعَرَفُوا أَنَّ الْكُفَّارَ عَايَنُوهُمْ وَلَمْ يَتَعَرَّضُوالَهُمْ قَالَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ هَذِهِ كَرَامَةٌ مِنَ الزَّاهِدِ وَلَا شَكَّ أَنَّهُ مِنَ الْخَوَاصِّ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓara ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-al-wazīru dandānu anna ʿasākira al-kuffāri wa-ʿarafū anna al-kuffāra ʿāyanūhum wa-lam yataʿarraḍū lahum qāla al-wazīru dandānu wa-allāhi inna hādhihi karāmatun mina al-zāhidi wa-lā shakka annahu mina al-khawāṣṣi
sentences.l: And when Ḍawʾ al-Makān and the vizier Dandān looked that the armies of the infidels [...], and knew that the infidels had eyed them and not meddled with them, the vizier Dandān said: By God, this is a wonder-of-grace from the ascetic, and no doubt he is of the special-ones.
sentences.i: When Ḍawʾ al-Makān and the vizier Dandān looked upon the infidel armies, and saw that the infidels had them in plain sight and yet left them alone, the vizier Dandān said, “By God, this is a wonder worked by the holy man; beyond doubt he is one of God's elect.”
sentences.n: The print has هذة, a misprint for هذه, corrected here. نظر … ان عساكر الكفار is doubtful as printed: the ان has nothing to complete it, and may be a slip for الى, “looked at”. It is kept as printed and pointed anna, “that”, and the sentence is translated by its likeliest sense, “looked upon the infidel armies”. naẓara, singular, comes before two subjects, then ʿarafū, plural, for the pair: Middle Arabic often counts two as a plural. يتعرضوالهم is set as one word, for yataʿarraḍū lahum. ʿāyana is to see with one's own eyes. A karāma is a wonder God works through a saint; al-khawāṣṣ, “the special ones”, are God's elect.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَاللَّهِ مَا أَظُنُّ الْكُفَّارَ إِلَّاعُمْيَانًا لِأَنَّنَا نَرَاهُمْ وَهُمْ لَا يَرَوْنَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-allāhi mā aẓunnu al-kuffāra illā ʿumyānan li-annanā narāhum wa-hum lā yarawnanā
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: By God, I do not think the infidels [anything] except blind-ones, because we see them and they do not see us.
sentences.i: “By God,” said Ḍawʾ al-Makān, “I can only think the infidels are blind, for we see them and they do not see us.”
sentences.n: الاعميانا is set as one word, for illā ʿumyānan, “but blind”. mā aẓunnu … illā, “I do not think … except”, is “I can only think”. The irony is the narrator's: the blind ones are the two Muslims.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُمَا فِى الثَّنَاءِ عَلَى الزَّاهِدِ وَتَعْدَادِ كَرَامَاتِهِ وَزُهْدِهِ وَعِبَادَاتِهِ وَإِذَا بِالْكُفَّارِ قَدْ هَجَمُوا عَلَيْهِمَا وَأَحَاطُوا بِهِمَا وَقَبَضُوا عَلَيْهِمَا
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā humā fī al-thanāʾi ʿalā al-zāhidi wa-taʿdādi karāmātihi wa-zuhdihi wa-ʿibādātihi wa-idhā bi-al-kuffāri qad hajamū ʿalayhimā wa-aḥāṭū bihimā wa-qabaḍū ʿalayhimā
sentences.l: And while they-two were in the praising of the ascetic and the counting-over of his wonders-of-grace and his asceticism and his devotions, and behold, the infidels had rushed upon them-two, and surrounded them-two, and seized upon them-two.
sentences.i: While the two of them were still praising the holy man and counting over his wonders, his austerity and his devotions, all at once the infidels fell upon them, surrounded them and laid hold of them.
sentences.n: wa-idhā bi-, “and behold”: after idhā the bi- only marks what suddenly appears. aḥāṭa bi-, “surround”, and qabaḍa ʿalā, “seize”, take their prepositions from the verb. Sajʿ: karāmātihi/ʿibādātihi, and ʿalayhimā/bihimā/ʿalayhimā. فى is printed with final ى for ي.

sentences.t: وَقَالُوا هَلْ مَعَكُمَا أَحَدٌ غَيْرُكُمَا فَنَقْبِضَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālū hal maʿakumā aḥadun ghayrukumā fa-naqbiḍa ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And they said: Is with you-two anyone other-than you-two, so-that we seize upon him?
sentences.i: “Is there anyone with you besides the two of you,” they said, “so that we may seize him too?”
sentences.n: The print has احل, a misprint for احد, corrected here. fa-naqbiḍa is subjunctive: a fa- answering a question gives “so that”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ أَمَا تَرَوْنَ هَذَا الرَّجُلَ الْآخَرَ الَّذِي بَيْنَ أَيْدِينَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru dandānu a-mā tarawna hādhā al-rajula al-ākhara alladhī bayna aydīnā
sentences.l: And the vizier Dandān said: Do you not see this other man who is between our hands?
sentences.i: The vizier Dandān said, “Do you not see this other man here before us?”
sentences.n: bayna aydīnā, “between our hands”, means “in front of us, right here”. Dandān still takes the old woman for a man.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمُ الْكُفَّارُ وَحَقِّ الْمَسِيحِ وَالرُّهْبَانِ وَالْجَاثَلِيقِ وَالْمُطْرَانِ إِنَّنَا لَمْ نَرَ أَحَدًا غَيْرَكُمَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahumu al-kuffāru wa-ḥaqqi al-masīḥi wa-al-ruhbāni wa-al-jāthalīqi wa-al-muṭrāni innanā lam nara aḥadan ghayrakumā
sentences.l: And the infidels said to them: By the right of the Messiah, and the monks, and the catholicos, and the metropolitan, we have not seen anyone other-than you-two.
sentences.i: The infidels answered, “By the truth of the Messiah, by the monks, the catholicos and the metropolitan, we have seen no one but you two.”
sentences.n: wa-ḥaqqi, “by the right of”, governs all four: the oath climbs the ranks of the Church, from monks to the catholicos, head of an Eastern church, and the metropolitan, an archbishop. lahum, plural, is said to the two men, the same counting of a pair as a plural.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ الَّذِي حَلَّ بِنَا عُقُوبَةٌ لَنَا مِنَ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-allāhi inna alladhī ḥalla binā ʿuqūbatun lanā mina allāhi taʿālā
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: By God, that-which has alighted at us is a punishment for us from God the Exalted.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān said, “By God, what has befallen us is a punishment laid on us by God Most High.”
sentences.n: ḥalla bi-, “alight at”, is said of a misfortune that comes down on someone: the verb chooses the bi-. The shadda on حلّ is the print's own.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
